question: Determine the vector of magnitude $6$ that is perpendicular to both $\vec{a}=\hat{i}+\hat{j}$ and $\vec{b}=\hat{j}+\hat{k}$ and whose $x$-component is positive; hence verify that the obtained vector has the required magnitude and direction.
explanation: Obtaining the Perpendicular DirectionA vector perpendicular to both $\vec{a}$ and $\vec{b}$ is parallel to $\vec{a}\times\vec{b}$.\\vec{a}\\times\\vec{b}=\\begin{vmatrix}\\hat{i} & \\hat{j} & \\hat{k}\\\\1 & 1 & 0\\\\0 & 1 & 1\\end{vmatrix}`\vec{a}\times\vec{b}=\hat{i}-\hat{j}+\hat{k}`Its magnitude is`|\vec{a}\times\vec{b}|=\sqrt{1^2+(-1)^2+1^2}=\sqrt{3}`Since the required vector has a positive $x$-component, the required unit direction is`\hat{n}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}(\hat{i}-\hat{j}+\hat{k})`Applying the Required MagnitudeThe vector of magnitude $6$ in this direction is`\vec{p}=6\hat{n}=\frac{6}{\sqrt{3}}(\hat{i}-\hat{j}+\hat{k})\vec{p}=2\sqrt{3}\hat{i}-2\sqrt{3}\hat{j}+2\sqrt{3}\hat{k}`Verification`\vec{p}\cdot\vec{a}=2\sqrt{3}-2\sqrt{3}=0\vec{p}\cdot\vec{b}=-2\sqrt{3}+2\sqrt{3}=0`Thus, $\vec{p}$ is perpendicular to both given vectors. Also,`|\vec{p}|=\sqrt{(2\sqrt{3})^2+(-2\sqrt{3})^2+(2\sqrt{3})^2}=\sqrt{36}=6`Final ResultThe required vector is $2\sqrt{3}\hat{i}-2\sqrt{3}\hat{j}+2\sqrt{3}\hat{k}$.

options.A: $\vec{p}=-2\sqrt{3}\hat{i}+2\sqrt{3}\hat{j}-2\sqrt{3}\hat{k}$; it is perpendicular to both given vectors and has magnitude $6$, but its $x$-component is negative.
options.C: $\vec{p}=2\hat{i}-2\hat{j}+2\hat{k}$; it is perpendicular to both vectors and has magnitude $6$.
options.D: $\vec{p}=2\sqrt{3}\hat{i}+2\sqrt{3}\hat{j}+2\sqrt{3}\hat{k}$; it has magnitude $6$ and is perpendicular to both vectors.
